title: Segment
summary: A segment is the part of a line between two endpoints — a straight piece with a definite length. Explore how segments are named, measured, and used as the sides of every polygon.

compareCandidate.label: Segment vs. line
compareCandidate.description: A segment has two endpoints and a fixed length; a line has no endpoints and goes on forever.

plainLanguageExplanation: A segment is the part of a line that sits between two endpoints — a straight, stop-at-both-ends piece. Because it stops, a segment has a definite length you can measure with a ruler. Name it with its two endpoints, like segment AB. Unlike a line or ray, a segment has no arrowheads — just two solid dots. Every side of a triangle, rectangle, or polygon is a segment, and the perimeter is the total of all the segment lengths.

keyFacts.label: Definition

keyFacts.label: Drawn as

keyFacts.label: Perimeter
keyFacts.value: The sum of the segment lengths

whyItMatters: Segments are the practical parts of geometry — the sides you measure, the edges you walk along, the lines on a ruler. Understanding segments turns abstract lines into things with size.
didYouKnow: A ruler is really a tool for measuring segments — the distance between two marks is always a segment, because it has a start and an end.
compareReason: Segments and lines look alike in drawings — comparing their endpoints makes the difference measurable and clear.
